conflicts.name: DICE_SLOTS
conflicts.finding: The areas describe three readers that accept different text. The document needs all three. (1) The Dice daemon writes plain numbers joined by commas (bin/dice:3656). (2) rinzler and runtron accept only that form: every item must be a number of 0 or more, and an empty item or a range fails (src/system/system.cpp:1470-1490). (3) The wrappers bin/rinzler and bin/runtron skip empty items and spaces (bin/rinzler:507-516). (4) bin/slice and bin/ci/bench_refresh_quiesce.py also accept ranges such as 4-7 (parse_slot_mask, bin/slice:1115-1137). The daemon sets the name for the program that it starts, and the strict C++ rule is the one that the product applies.

conflicts.name: SYSTEM_CONFIG
conflicts.finding: All areas agree on the product parser. The readers differ in how much of the text they understand, and the document should say so. rinzler and runtron parse every system option (src/system/system.cpp:1954-2052). The Python wrappers, bin/slice, bin/dice and the LSF bridge understand only --instance X,Y and --instance=X,Y, and bin/slice also a bare X,Y. notes: Method. The whole checkout (1420 tracked files) was searched, not only one area. Step 1: git grep for each of the 69 set-only names in every file. Step 2: git grep for each of the 10 names that only the documentation has. Step 3: new scans over every text file, compared with the union of 525 names: every getenv, setenv, unsetenv and putenv call in C, C++ and Rust (85 literal names, 11 calls with a name held in a variable); a Python syntax-tree scan of every Python file for environment access with a literal or a computed key (80 computed keys, all resolved to constants or loops that the inventory lists); every upper-case $NAME and ${NAME} that its file never assigns; every '?=', ifdef, ifndef and $(origin) in the four makefiles; every env key and every env., vars. and secrets. reference in the 13 workflows and lefthook.yml (parsed as YAML); every ENVIRONMENT, ENV{...} and 'ENV name' use in the CMake files; every write to the GITHUB_ENV and GITHUB_PATH files; every quoted upper-case name; every name with a known prefix (TRON_, RZ_, POS_, DICE_, SLICE_, HF_, CARGO_, NIX_ and others, about 100 prefixes in total). Step 4: the callers of about 45 helper functions that read the environment were listed for the whole tree and compared with the helper list. Step 5: a script printed values and defaults side by side for the 204 names that two or more areas report, and all of them were read. Result for missing names: none. Every name that TRON code reads or sets by name is in the union. The only addition is one reader of PATH (see 'missing'). Result for role changes: none. No set-only name has a TRON reader that takes the value from the caller's environment. Four cases look like reads and are not: __NIX_USERNAME (the same shell hook reads its own value), TEST_RUNNER_RC (a test fixture reads it from a JSON file), XDG_DATA_HOME (a test reads the workflow YAML text) and CARGO_HOME, CCACHE_TEMPDIR, CABAL_DIR (the same script expands the value that it has just assigned). Dead exports. Five names are exported and nothing in the checkout reads them: LLVM_LIB_DIR, CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR, CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER as environment variables (flake.nix:1169-1170, :1868-1869, :1903-1908), and TRON_BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY (bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py:202). They are candidates for removal and should not be presented as controls. Error in an area note. The notes of cpp-rinzler-runtron list TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE, POS_PREQUANT_CACHE and POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE among names that rinzler and runtron read. That is wrong at this commit: only t/t_prequant_cache.cpp includes the header. The same note says its call chains were not traced. The other names in that list are in sources of the tron library or of the full scheduler objects. Which program runs which reader.
